------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  pwEquivalence : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  pwEquivalence eq₁ eq₂ = record
    -- [case] Reflexivity: since ≈₁ is reflexive, a ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is reflexive, b ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a, b).
    { refl = (λ {x} → IsEquivalence.refl eq₁ , IsEquivalence.refl eq₂)
    -- [case] Symmetry: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b'). Since ≈₁ is symmetric, a' ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is symmetric, b' ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a', b') ≋ (a, b).
    ; sym = (λ {x} {y} z → IsEquivalence.sym eq₁ (z .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.sym eq₂ (z .proj₂))
    -- [case] Transitivity: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b') and (a', b') ≋ (a'', b''). Since ≈₁ is transitive, a ≈₁ a''. Since ≈₂ is transitive, b ≈₂ b''. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a'', b'').
    ; trans = (λ {x} {y} {z} z₁ z₂ → IsEquivalence.trans eq₁ (z₁ .proj₁) (z₂ .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.trans eq₂ (z₁ .proj₂) (z₂ .proj₂))
    }

  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (p q : B) → p ≈₂ q → p ≤₂ q
  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ tot p q eq =
    let
      -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_. Extract the partial order structure on B; totality is not used.
      po : IsPartialOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_
      po = (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder tot)
      -- Step 2: The partial order contains a preorder for ≤₂ with equivalence ≈₂. Its reflexivity field: x ≈₂ y implies x ≤₂ y.
      refl₂ : _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_
      refl₂ = (λ {x} {y} z → Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) z)
      -- Step 3: Apply the reflexivity field to x = p and y = q with eq : p ≈₂ q, yielding p ≤₂ q.
      r : p ≤₂ q
      r = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) eq)
    in
    -- Step 4: Since p and q were arbitrary and the assumption was the total order structure, for every p, q in B, p ≈₂ q implies p ≤₂ q.
    r

  lexReflexive : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → (x ≋ y) → (x ≤ₗₑₓ y)
  -- Step 2: pointwise on pairs gives a ≈₁ a' and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 3: (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b') means a ≤₁ a' with not (a ≈₁ a'), or a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b'.
  -- Step 4: the first alternative needs not (a ≈₁ a'), which fails, so take the second alternative.
  -- Step 5: b ≤₂ b' follows from reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ applied to ≤₂ and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 6: the second alternative holds, so (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b'); x and y were arbitrary with x ≋ y.
  lexReflexive t₁ t₂ (a , b) (a' , b') (e₁ , e₂) = (inj₂ (e₁ , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂)) e₂))

  strictTrans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: assume a < c and c < e; unpack into a ≤ c, not (a ≈ c), c ≤ e, not (c ≈ e).
  -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤ gives a ≤ e.
  -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈ e); suppose for contradiction that a ≈ e.
  -- Step 4: symmetry gives e ≈ a; reflexivity gives e ≤ e; ≤ respects ≈ in its second argument, so e ≤ a.
  -- Step 5: c ≤ e and e ≤ a give c ≤ a by transitivity.
  -- Step 6: a ≤ c and c ≤ a give a ≈ c by antisymmetry.
  -- Step 7: this contradicts not (a ≈ c) from Step 1, so a ≈ e is false.
  -- Step 8: therefore not (a ≈ e); with a ≤ e from Step 2, this is exactly a < e.
  strictTrans t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) (ce≤ , ce≉) = (IsTotalOrder.trans t ac≤ ce≤ , λ h → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.antisym t ac≤ (IsTotalOrder.trans t ce≤ (IsTotalOrder.reflexive t (IsEquivalence.sym (IsTotalOrder.isEquivalence t) h)))))

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  strictFromEqRight : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → c ≈₁ e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: unfolding the strict order, a < c means a ≤ c and not (a ≈ c), so the goal a < e is a ≤ e and not (a ≈ e).
  strictFromEqRight t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) ce≈ =
    -- Step 7: combining step 2 (a ≤ e) with step 6 (not (a ≈ e)) gives a < e.
    -- Step 2: a ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ e give a ≤₁ e, by the second part of leRespectsEq.
    {!!} ,
    -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈₁ e); suppose a ≈₁ e for contradiction.
    {!!}

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K --safe #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  pwEquivalence : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  pwEquivalence eq₁ eq₂ = record
    -- [case] Reflexivity: since ≈₁ is reflexive, a ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is reflexive, b ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a, b).
    { refl = (λ {x} → IsEquivalence.refl eq₁ , IsEquivalence.refl eq₂)
    -- [case] Symmetry: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b'). Since ≈₁ is symmetric, a' ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is symmetric, b' ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a', b') ≋ (a, b).
    ; sym = (λ {x} {y} z → IsEquivalence.sym eq₁ (z .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.sym eq₂ (z .proj₂))
    -- [case] Transitivity: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b') and (a', b') ≋ (a'', b''). Since ≈₁ is transitive, a ≈₁ a''. Since ≈₂ is transitive, b ≈₂ b''. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a'', b'').
    ; trans = (λ {x} {y} {z} z₁ z₂ → IsEquivalence.trans eq₁ (z₁ .proj₁) (z₂ .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.trans eq₂ (z₁ .proj₂) (z₂ .proj₂))
    }

  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (p q : B) → p ≈₂ q → p ≤₂ q
  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ tot p q eq =
    let
      -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_. Extract the partial order structure on B; totality is not used.
      po : IsPartialOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_
      po = (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder tot)
      -- Step 2: The partial order contains a preorder for ≤₂ with equivalence ≈₂. Its reflexivity field: x ≈₂ y implies x ≤₂ y.
      refl₂ : _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_
      refl₂ = (λ {x} {y} z → Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) z)
      -- Step 3: Apply the reflexivity field to x = p and y = q with eq : p ≈₂ q, yielding p ≤₂ q.
      r : p ≤₂ q
      r = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) eq)
    in
    -- Step 4: Since p and q were arbitrary and the assumption was the total order structure, for every p, q in B, p ≈₂ q implies p ≤₂ q.
    r

  lexReflexive : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → (x ≋ y) → (x ≤ₗₑₓ y)
  -- Step 2: pointwise on pairs gives a ≈₁ a' and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 3: (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b') means a ≤₁ a' with not (a ≈₁ a'), or a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b'.
  -- Step 4: the first alternative needs not (a ≈₁ a'), which fails, so take the second alternative.
  -- Step 5: b ≤₂ b' follows from reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ applied to ≤₂ and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 6: the second alternative holds, so (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b'); x and y were arbitrary with x ≋ y.
  lexReflexive t₁ t₂ (a , b) (a' , b') (e₁ , e₂) = (inj₂ (e₁ , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂)) e₂))

  strictTrans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: assume a < c and c < e; unpack into a ≤ c, not (a ≈ c), c ≤ e, not (c ≈ e).
  -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤ gives a ≤ e.
  -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈ e); suppose for contradiction that a ≈ e.
  -- Step 4: symmetry gives e ≈ a; reflexivity gives e ≤ e; ≤ respects ≈ in its second argument, so e ≤ a.
  -- Step 5: c ≤ e and e ≤ a give c ≤ a by transitivity.
  -- Step 6: a ≤ c and c ≤ a give a ≈ c by antisymmetry.
  -- Step 7: this contradicts not (a ≈ c) from Step 1, so a ≈ e is false.
  -- Step 8: therefore not (a ≈ e); with a ≤ e from Step 2, this is exactly a < e.
  strictTrans t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) (ce≤ , ce≉) = (IsTotalOrder.trans t ac≤ ce≤ , λ h → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.antisym t ac≤ (IsTotalOrder.trans t ce≤ (IsTotalOrder.reflexive t (IsEquivalence.sym (IsTotalOrder.isEquivalence t) h)))))

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  strictFromEqRight : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → c ≈₁ e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: unfolding the strict order, a < c means a ≤ c and not (a ≈ c), so the goal a < e is a ≤ e and not (a ≈ e).
  strictFromEqRight t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) ce≈ =
    -- Step 7: combining step 2 (a ≤ e) with step 6 (not (a ≈ e)) gives a < e.
    -- Step 2: a ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ e give a ≤₁ e, by the second part of leRespectsEq.
    (IsPartialOrder.≤-respʳ-≈ (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) ce≈ ac≤) ,
    -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈₁ e); suppose a ≈₁ e for contradiction.
    (λ a≈e → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.Eq.trans t a≈e (IsTotalOrder.Eq.sym t ce≈)))

-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)

  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_

    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_

    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)

                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_

    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------

  -- dsp: lemmas
  pwEquivalence : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_

    -- [case] Reflexivity: since ≈₁ is reflexive, a ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is reflexive, b ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a, b).
    { refl = (λ {x} → IsEquivalence.refl eq₁ , IsEquivalence.refl eq₂)
    -- [case] Symmetry: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b'). Since ≈₁ is symmetric, a' ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is symmetric, b' ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a', b') ≋ (a, b).
    ; sym = (λ {x} {y} z → IsEquivalence.sym eq₁ (z .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.sym eq₂ (z .proj₂))
    -- [case] Transitivity: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b') and (a', b') ≋ (a'', b''). Since ≈₁ is transitive, a ≈₁ a''. Since ≈₂ is transitive, b ≈₂ b''. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a'', b'').
    ; trans = (λ {x} {y} {z} z₁ z₂ → IsEquivalence.trans eq₁ (z₁ .proj₁) (z₂ .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.trans eq₂ (z₁ .proj₂) (z₂ .proj₂))
    }

  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (p q : B) → p ≈₂ q → p ≤₂ q
  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ tot p q eq =
    let
      -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_. Extract the partial order structure on B; totality is not used.
      po : IsPartialOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_
      po = (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder tot)
      -- Step 2: The partial order contains a preorder for ≤₂ with equivalence ≈₂. Its reflexivity field: x ≈₂ y implies x ≤₂ y.
      refl₂ : _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_
      refl₂ = (λ {x} {y} z → Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) z)
      -- Step 3: Apply the reflexivity field to x = p and y = q with eq : p ≈₂ q, yielding p ≤₂ q.
      r : p ≤₂ q
      r = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) eq)
    in
    -- Step 4: Since p and q were arbitrary and the assumption was the total order structure, for every p, q in B, p ≈₂ q implies p ≤₂ q.
    r

  lexReflexive : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → (x ≋ y) → (x ≤ₗₑₓ y)
  -- Step 2: pointwise on pairs gives a ≈₁ a' and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 3: (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b') means a ≤₁ a' with not (a ≈₁ a'), or a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b'.
  -- Step 4: the first alternative needs not (a ≈₁ a'), which fails, so take the second alternative.
  -- Step 5: b ≤₂ b' follows from reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ applied to ≤₂ and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 6: the second alternative holds, so (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b'); x and y were arbitrary with x ≋ y.

  strictTrans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: assume a < c and c < e; unpack into a ≤ c, not (a ≈ c), c ≤ e, not (c ≈ e).
  -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤ gives a ≤ e.
  -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈ e); suppose for contradiction that a ≈ e.
  -- Step 4: symmetry gives e ≈ a; reflexivity gives e ≤ e; ≤ respects ≈ in its second argument, so e ≤ a.
  -- Step 5: c ≤ e and e ≤ a give c ≤ a by transitivity.
  -- Step 6: a ≤ c and c ≤ a give a ≈ c by antisymmetry.
  -- Step 7: this contradicts not (a ≈ c) from Step 1, so a ≈ e is false.
  -- Step 8: therefore not (a ≈ e); with a ≤ e from Step 2, this is exactly a < e.

  strictFromEqRight : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → c ≈₁ e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: unfolding the strict order, a < c means a ≤ c and not (a ≈ c), so the goal a < e is a ≤ e and not (a ≈ e).

    -- Step 7: combining step 2 (a ≤ e) with step 6 (not (a ≈ e)) gives a < e.
    -- Step 2: a ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ e give a ≤₁ e, by the second part of leRespectsEq.

    -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈₁ e); suppose a ≈₁ e for contradiction.
    (λ a≈e → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.Eq.trans t a≈e (IsTotalOrder.Eq.sym t ce≈)))

  strictFromEqLeft : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → a ≈₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  pwEquivalence : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_
  pwEquivalence eq₁ eq₂ = record
    -- [case] Reflexivity: since ≈₁ is reflexive, a ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is reflexive, b ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a, b).
    { refl = (λ {x} → IsEquivalence.refl eq₁ , IsEquivalence.refl eq₂)
    -- [case] Symmetry: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b'). Since ≈₁ is symmetric, a' ≈₁ a. Since ≈₂ is symmetric, b' ≈₂ b. Both components hold, so (a', b') ≋ (a, b).
    ; sym = (λ {x} {y} z → IsEquivalence.sym eq₁ (z .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.sym eq₂ (z .proj₂))
    -- [case] Transitivity: suppose (a, b) ≋ (a', b') and (a', b') ≋ (a'', b''). Since ≈₁ is transitive, a ≈₁ a''. Since ≈₂ is transitive, b ≈₂ b''. Both components hold, so (a, b) ≋ (a'', b'').
    ; trans = (λ {x} {y} {z} z₁ z₂ → IsEquivalence.trans eq₁ (z₁ .proj₁) (z₂ .proj₁) , IsEquivalence.trans eq₂ (z₁ .proj₂) (z₂ .proj₂))
    }

  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ : IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (p q : B) → p ≈₂ q → p ≤₂ q
  reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ tot p q eq =
    let
      -- Step 1: Assume IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_. Extract the partial order structure on B; totality is not used.
      po : IsPartialOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_
      po = (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder tot)
      -- Step 2: The partial order contains a preorder for ≤₂ with equivalence ≈₂. Its reflexivity field: x ≈₂ y implies x ≤₂ y.
      refl₂ : _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_
      refl₂ = (λ {x} {y} z → Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) z)
      -- Step 3: Apply the reflexivity field to x = p and y = q with eq : p ≈₂ q, yielding p ≤₂ q.
      r : p ≤₂ q
      r = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) eq)
    in
    -- Step 4: Since p and q were arbitrary and the assumption was the total order structure, for every p, q in B, p ≈₂ q implies p ≤₂ q.
    r

  lexReflexive : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → (x y : A × B) → (x ≋ y) → (x ≤ₗₑₓ y)
  -- Step 2: pointwise on pairs gives a ≈₁ a' and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 3: (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b') means a ≤₁ a' with not (a ≈₁ a'), or a ≈₁ a' with b ≤₂ b'.
  -- Step 4: the first alternative needs not (a ≈₁ a'), which fails, so take the second alternative.
  -- Step 5: b ≤₂ b' follows from reflexiveOnEquivalence₂ applied to ≤₂ and b ≈₂ b'.
  -- Step 6: the second alternative holds, so (a, b) ≤ₗₑₓ (a', b'); x and y were arbitrary with x ≋ y.
  lexReflexive t₁ t₂ (a , b) (a' , b') (e₁ , e₂) = (inj₂ (e₁ , Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t₂)) e₂))

  strictTrans : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: assume a < c and c < e; unpack into a ≤ c, not (a ≈ c), c ≤ e, not (c ≈ e).
  -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤ gives a ≤ e.
  -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈ e); suppose for contradiction that a ≈ e.
  -- Step 4: symmetry gives e ≈ a; reflexivity gives e ≤ e; ≤ respects ≈ in its second argument, so e ≤ a.
  -- Step 5: c ≤ e and e ≤ a give c ≤ a by transitivity.
  -- Step 6: a ≤ c and c ≤ a give a ≈ c by antisymmetry.
  -- Step 7: this contradicts not (a ≈ c) from Step 1, so a ≈ e is false.
  -- Step 8: therefore not (a ≈ e); with a ≤ e from Step 2, this is exactly a < e.
  strictTrans t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) (ce≤ , ce≉) = (IsTotalOrder.trans t ac≤ ce≤ , λ h → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.antisym t ac≤ (IsTotalOrder.trans t ce≤ (IsTotalOrder.reflexive t (IsEquivalence.sym (IsTotalOrder.isEquivalence t) h)))))

  strictFromEqRight : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c → c ≈₁ e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: unfolding the strict order, a < c means a ≤ c and not (a ≈ c), so the goal a < e is a ≤ e and not (a ≈ e).
  strictFromEqRight t a c e (ac≤ , ac≉) ce≈ =
    -- Step 7: combining step 2 (a ≤ e) with step 6 (not (a ≈ e)) gives a < e.
    -- Step 2: a ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ e give a ≤₁ e, by the second part of leRespectsEq.
    (IsPartialOrder.≤-respʳ-≈ (IsTotalOrder.isPartialOrder t) ce≈ ac≤) ,
    -- Step 3: it remains to show not (a ≈₁ e); suppose a ≈₁ e for contradiction.
    (λ a≈e → ac≉ (IsTotalOrder.Eq.trans t a≈e (IsTotalOrder.Eq.sym t ce≈)))

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  strictFromEqLeft : IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → (a c e : A) → a ≈₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ c e → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a e
  -- Step 1: unfolding the strict order, the goal a < e is a ≤ e and not (a ≈ e).
  -- Step 2: the hypothesis c < e gives c ≤ e and not (c ≈ e).
  strictFromEqLeft t a c e a≈c (ce≤ , ce≉) =
    -- Step 3: since a ≈ c, the left respect of ≤ over ≈ turns c ≤ e into a ≤ e.
    {!!} ,
    -- Step 4: suppose, for contradiction, that a ≈ e.
    -- Step 5: symmetry gives c ≈ a, and transitivity with a ≈ e gives c ≈ e.
    -- Step 6: this contradicts not (c ≈ e) from step 2, so not (a ≈ e).
    -- Step 7: combining step 3 (a ≤ e) with step 6 (not (a ≈ e)) gives a < e.
    (λ a≈e → {!!})

open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions

private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

  postulate

  postulate

  postulate
    ×-lex-total : Decidable _≈₁_ → Total _≤₁_ → Total _≤₂_ → Total _≤ₗₑₓ_

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-isTotalOrder : Decidable _≈₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsTotalOrder _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  -- Step 1: ≤_lex is reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric and total with respect to ≈_pw, and respects ≈_pw.
  ×-isTotalOrder dec-≈₁ tot₁ tot₂ = record
    { isPartialOrder = record
        { isPreorder = record
            -- Step 2: ≈_pw is an equivalence relation on A × B.
            { isEquivalence = record
                -- Step 3: reflexivity: for any (a,b), (a,b) ≈_pw (a,b).
                { refl = {!!}
                -- Step 4: symmetry: from (a,b) ≈_pw (a',b') infer (a',b') ≈_pw (a,b).
                ; sym = {!!}
                -- Step 5: transitivity: from (a,b) ≈_pw (a',b') and (a',b') ≈_pw (a'',b'') infer (a,b) ≈_pw (a'',b'').
                ; trans = {!!}
                }
            -- Step 14-15: for every (a,b), (a,b) ≤_lex (a,b).
            ; reflexive = {!!}
            -- Step 16: if (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) and (c,d) ≤_lex (e,f), then (a,b) ≤_lex (e,f).
            ; trans = {!!}
            }
        -- Step 21: if (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) and (c,d) ≤_lex (a,b), then (a,b) ≈_pw (c,d).
        ; antisym = {!!}
        }
    -- Step 26: assuming ≈₁ is decidable, either (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) or (c,d) ≤_lex (a,b).
    ; total = {!!}
    }

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  postulate
    ≋-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → IsEquivalence _≈₂_ → IsEquivalence _≋_

  postulate
    ×-lex-resp-left : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≋ q → p ≤ₗₑₓ r → q ≤ₗₑₓ r

  postulate
    ×-lex-resp-right : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≋ r → p ≤ₗₑₓ r

  postulate
    ×-lex-refl : _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q : A × B} → p ≋ q → p ≤ₗₑₓ q

  postulate
    ×-lex-trans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≤ₗₑₓ r → p ≤ₗₑₓ r

  postulate
    ×-lex-antisymm : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≤ₗₑₓ p → p ≋ q

  postulate
    ×-lex-total : Decidable _≈₁_ → Total _≤₁_ → Total _≤₂_ → Total _≤ₗₑₓ_

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-isTotalOrder : Decidable _≈₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → IsTotalOrder _≈₂_ _≤₂_ → IsTotalOrder _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  -- Step 1: ≤_lex is reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric and total with respect to ≈_pw, and respects ≈_pw.
  ×-isTotalOrder dec-≈₁ tot₁ tot₂ = record
    { isPartialOrder = record
        { isPreorder = record
            -- Step 2: ≈_pw is an equivalence relation on A × B.
            { isEquivalence = record
                -- Step 3: reflexivity: for any (a,b), (a,b) ≈_pw (a,b).
                { refl = {!!}
                -- Step 4: symmetry: from (a,b) ≈_pw (a',b') infer (a',b') ≈_pw (a,b).
                ; sym = {!!}
                -- Step 5: transitivity: from (a,b) ≈_pw (a',b') and (a',b') ≈_pw (a'',b'') infer (a,b) ≈_pw (a'',b'').
                ; trans = {!!}
                }
            -- Step 14-15: for every (a,b), (a,b) ≤_lex (a,b).
            ; reflexive = {!!}
            -- Step 16: if (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) and (c,d) ≤_lex (e,f), then (a,b) ≤_lex (e,f).
            ; trans = {!!}
            }
        -- Step 21: if (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) and (c,d) ≤_lex (a,b), then (a,b) ≈_pw (c,d).
        ; antisym = {!!}
        }
    -- Step 26: assuming ≈₁ is decidable, either (a,b) ≤_lex (c,d) or (c,d) ≤_lex (a,b).
    ; total = {!!}
    }

### Example 1

Informal statement:
For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-identityr : (n : Nat) → n + 0 ≡ n

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + 0 reduces to 0, so the two sides are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: suppose n + 0 = n. Then (suc n) + 0 reduces to suc (n + 0),
and rewriting with the induction hypothesis turns this into suc n.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 2

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers m and n, m + suc n = suc (m + n).

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-suc : (m n : Nat) → m + suc n ≡ suc (m + n)

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on m, holding n fixed.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + suc n reduces to suc n, and suc (0 + n) also reduces to suc n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + suc n = suc (m + n). Then (suc m) + suc n reduces
to suc (m + suc n), which by the induction hypothesis equals suc (suc (m + n)),
which is suc ((suc m) + n).
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 3

Informal statement:
Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-comm : (m n : Nat) → m + n ≡ n + m

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="lemma" name="plusZeroRight">

</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="plusSucRight">
We also need that m + suc n = suc (m + n) for all m and n; again a separate
induction, recorded as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="induction">
Now argue by induction on m.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + n reduces to n, and n + 0 equals n by the first lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + n = n + m. Then suc m + n reduces to suc (m + n),
which by the hypothesis is suc (n + m), which by the second lemma is n + suc m.
</STEP>

<STEP index="5" kind="case">

</STEP>
<STEP index="6" kind="case">
Case 1, subcase 1b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. Since q₁ ≈₁ r₁, we have q₁ ≤₁ r₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by the lemma ltLeTrans, applied to p₁ <₁ q₁ and q₁ ≤₁ r₁. So p ≤ₗₑₓ r, since its first disjunct holds.
</STEP>
<STEP index="7" kind="case">
Case 2: p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and p₂ ≤₂ q₂. Subcase 2a: q₁ <₁ r₁. Since p₁ ≈₁ q₁, we have p₁ ≤₁ q₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by the lemma leLtTrans, applied to p₁ ≤₁ q₁ and q₁ <₁ r₁. So p ≤ₗₑₓ r, since its first disjunct holds.
</STEP>
<STEP index="8" kind="case">
Case 2, subcase 2b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. From p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and q₁ ≈₁ r₁, transitivity of the equivalence ≈₁ gives p₁ ≈₁ r₁. From p₂ ≤₂ q₂ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂, transitivity of ≤₂ gives p₂ ≤₂ r₂. So p₁ ≈₁ r₁ and p₂ ≤₂ r₂, which is the second disjunct, and hence p ≤ₗₑₓ r.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  postulate
    ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c

  postulate
    leLtTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → a ≤₁ b → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ b c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-trans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≤ₗₑₓ r → p ≤ₗₑₓ r
  -- Step 4: split on the two ways p ≤ₗₑₓ q can hold, then on the two ways q ≤ₗₑₓ r can hold.
  -- Case 1, subcase 1a: p₁ <₁ q₁ and q₁ <₁ r₁ give p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₁ qr) = {!!}
  -- Case 1, subcase 1b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. Since q₁ ≈₁ r₁, we have q₁ ≤₁ r₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = {!!}
  -- Case 2, subcase 2a: p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and p₂ ≤₂ q₂, with q₁ <₁ r₁. Since p₁ ≈₁ q₁, we have p₁ ≤₁ q₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by leLtTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₁ qr) = {!!}
  -- Case 2, subcase 2b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. From p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and q₁ ≈₁ r₁, transitivity of ≈₁ gives p₁ ≈₁ r₁. From p₂ ≤₂ q₂ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂, transitivity of ≤₂ gives p₂ ≤₂ r₂. So p ≤ₗₑₓ r via the second disjunct.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = {!!}

ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
-- 1. By definition, a <₁ b means a ≤₁ b and not (a ≈₁ b).
-- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.
-- 3. It remains to show not (a ≈₁ c). We argue by contradiction, so assume a ≈₁ c.
-- 4. By symmetry of ≈₁, the assumption a ≈₁ c gives c ≈₁ a.
-- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.
-- 6. We now have a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ a. By antisymmetry of the partial order, a ≈₁ b.
-- 7. This contradicts the fact from step 1 that not (a ≈₁ b). So the assumption a ≈₁ c is false.
-- 8. Hence not (a ≈₁ c). Together with a ≤₁ c from step 2, this gives a <₁ c.
ltLeTrans po resp (a≤b , a≉b) b≤c = {!!}

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂

-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c

  -- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.
  -- 3. It remains to show not (a ≈₁ c). We argue by contradiction, so assume a ≈₁ c.
  -- 4. By symmetry of ≈₁, the assumption a ≈₁ c gives c ≈₁ a.
  -- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.
  -- 6. We now have a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ a. By antisymmetry of the partial order, a ≈₁ b.
  -- 7. This contradicts the fact from step 1 that not (a ≈₁ b). So the assumption a ≈₁ c is false.
  -- 8. Hence not (a ≈₁ c). Together with a ≤₁ c from step 2, this gives a <₁ c.
  ltLeTrans po resp (a≤b , a≉b) b≤c = {!!}

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- 1. By definition, a <₁ b means a ≤₁ b and not (a ≈₁ b).
  -- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.
  -- 3. It remains to show not (a ≈₁ c). We argue by contradiction, so assume a ≈₁ c.
  -- 4. By symmetry of ≈₁, the assumption a ≈₁ c gives c ≈₁ a.
  -- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.
  -- 6. We now have a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ a. By antisymmetry of the partial order, a ≈₁ b.
  -- 7. This contradicts the fact from step 1 that not (a ≈₁ b). So the assumption a ≈₁ c is false.
  -- 8. Hence not (a ≈₁ c). Together with a ≤₁ c from step 2, this gives a <₁ c.
  ltLeTrans po resp (a≤b , a≉b) b≤c = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → a≉b (IsPartialOrder.antisym po a≤b (resp .proj₁ (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po)) z) b≤c))))

You are a mathematician writing informal proofs that will later be formalised
in Agda by another agent. Write in ordinary mathematical English. Do not write
Agda. Do not skip steps by saying "clearly" or "trivially".


Follow the format of these examples exactly.

### Example 1

Informal statement:
For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-identityr : (n : Nat) → n + 0 ≡ n

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + 0 reduces to 0, so the two sides are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: suppose n + 0 = n. Then (suc n) + 0 reduces to suc (n + 0),
and rewriting with the induction hypothesis turns this into suc n.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 2

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers m and n, m + suc n = suc (m + n).

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-suc : (m n : Nat) → m + suc n ≡ suc (m + n)

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on m, holding n fixed.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + suc n reduces to suc n, and suc (0 + n) also reduces to suc n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + suc n = suc (m + n). Then (suc m) + suc n reduces
to suc (m + suc n), which by the induction hypothesis equals suc (suc (m + n)),
which is suc ((suc m) + n).
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 3

Informal statement:
Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-comm : (m n : Nat) → m + n ≡ n + m

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="lemma" name="plusZeroRight">
First we need that n + 0 = n for every n; this is a separate induction and we
record it as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="plusSucRight">
We also need that m + suc n = suc (m + n) for all m and n; again a separate
induction, recorded as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="induction">
Now argue by induction on m.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + n reduces to n, and n + 0 equals n by the first lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + n = n + m. Then suc m + n reduces to suc (m + n),
which by the hypothesis is suc (n + m), which by the second lemma is n + suc m.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>


### Now your turn

        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →

  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂

    -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤₁ applied to a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first component needed for a <₁ c.

--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- 1. By definition, a <₁ b means a ≤₁ b and not (a ≈₁ b).
  -- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.

  -- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.

  leLtTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → a ≤₁ b → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ b c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- Step 1: by definition, b <₁ c means b ≤₁ c and not (b ≈₁ c). We record both facts for use below.
  leLtTrans po resp a≤b (b≤c , b≉c) =
    -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤₁ applied to a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first component needed for a <₁ c.
    (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → b≉c (IsPartialOrder.antisym po b≤c (resp .proj₂ z a≤b))))

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-trans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≤ₗₑₓ r → p ≤ₗₑₓ r
  -- Step 4: split on the two ways p ≤ₗₑₓ q can hold, then on the two ways q ≤ₗₑₓ r can hold.
  -- Case 1, subcase 1a: p₁ <₁ q₁ and q₁ <₁ r₁ give p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₁ qr) = (inj₁ (ltLeTrans po₁ resp₁ pq (qr .proj₁)))
  -- Case 1, subcase 1b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. Since q₁ ≈₁ r₁, we have q₁ ≤₁ r₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = (inj₁ (ltLeTrans po₁ resp₁ pq (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁) qe)))
  -- Case 2, subcase 2a: p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and p₂ ≤₂ q₂, with q₁ <₁ r₁. Since p₁ ≈₁ q₁, we have p₁ ≤₁ q₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by leLtTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₁ qr) = (inj₁ (leLtTrans po₁ resp₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁) pe) qr))
  -- Case 2, subcase 2b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. From p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and q₁ ≈₁ r₁, transitivity of ≈₁ gives p₁ ≈₁ r₁. From p₂ ≤₂ q₂ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂, transitivity of ≤₂ gives p₂ ≤₂ r₂. So p ≤ₗₑₓ r via the second disjunct.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = (inj₂ (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁)) pe qe , trans₂ pl ql))

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The Agda standard library
--
-- Lexicographic products of binary relations
------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The definition of lexicographic product used here is suitable if
-- the left-hand relation is a (non-strict) partial order.

{-# OPTIONS --without-K #-}

module Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.NonStrict where

open import Data.Product.Base using (_×_; _,_; proj₁; proj₂)
open import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Pointwise.NonDependent as Pointwise
  using (Pointwise)
import Data.Product.Relation.Binary.Lex.Strict as Strict
open import Data.Sum.Base using (inj₁; inj₂)
open import Level using (Level)
open import Relation.Binary.Core using (Rel; _⇒_)
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles
  using (Poset; DecTotalOrder; TotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Structures
  using (IsPartialOrder; IsEquivalence; IsTotalOrder; IsDecTotalOrder)
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions
  using (Transitive; Symmetric; Decidable; Antisymmetric; Total; Trichotomous
        ; Irreflexive; Asymmetric; _Respects₂_; tri<; tri>; tri≈)
open import Relation.Binary.Consequences
import Relation.Binary.Construct.NonStrictToStrict as Conv


private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level
    A : Set a
    B : Set b

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Definition

×-Lex : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂) (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃) →
        Rel (A × B) _
×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ = Strict.×-Lex _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Properties

×-reflexive : (_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁) (_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂)
              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →
              _≈₂_ ⇒ _≤₂_ →
              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)
×-reflexive _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_ refl₂ =
  Strict.×-reflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_) _≤₂_ refl₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-decidable dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁ dec-≤₂ =
    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_
  ×-respects₂ eq₁ resp₁ resp₂ =
    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- 1. By definition, a <₁ b means a ≤₁ b and not (a ≈₁ b).
  -- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.
  -- 3. It remains to show not (a ≈₁ c). We argue by contradiction, so assume a ≈₁ c.
  -- 4. By symmetry of ≈₁, the assumption a ≈₁ c gives c ≈₁ a.
  -- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.
  -- 6. We now have a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ a. By antisymmetry of the partial order, a ≈₁ b.
  -- 7. This contradicts the fact from step 1 that not (a ≈₁ b). So the assumption a ≈₁ c is false.
  -- 8. Hence not (a ≈₁ c). Together with a ≤₁ c from step 2, this gives a <₁ c.
  ltLeTrans po resp (a≤b , a≉b) b≤c = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → a≉b (IsPartialOrder.antisym po a≤b (resp .proj₁ (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po)) z) b≤c))))

  leLtTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → a ≤₁ b → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ b c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- Step 1: by definition, b <₁ c means b ≤₁ c and not (b ≈₁ c). We record both facts for use below.
  leLtTrans po resp a≤b (b≤c , b≉c) =
    -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤₁ applied to a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first component needed for a <₁ c.
    (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → b≉c (IsPartialOrder.antisym po b≤c (resp .proj₂ z a≤b))))

  -- dsp: end of lemmas
  ×-lex-trans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ → ∀ {p q r : A × B} → p ≤ₗₑₓ q → q ≤ₗₑₓ r → p ≤ₗₑₓ r
  -- Step 4: split on the two ways p ≤ₗₑₓ q can hold, then on the two ways q ≤ₗₑₓ r can hold.
  -- Case 1, subcase 1a: p₁ <₁ q₁ and q₁ <₁ r₁ give p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₁ qr) = (inj₁ (ltLeTrans po₁ resp₁ pq (qr .proj₁)))
  -- Case 1, subcase 1b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. Since q₁ ≈₁ r₁, we have q₁ ≤₁ r₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by ltLeTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₁ pq) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = (inj₁ (ltLeTrans po₁ resp₁ pq (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁) qe)))
  -- Case 2, subcase 2a: p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and p₂ ≤₂ q₂, with q₁ <₁ r₁. Since p₁ ≈₁ q₁, we have p₁ ≤₁ q₁. Then p₁ <₁ r₁ by leLtTrans, so p ≤ₗₑₓ r since its first disjunct holds.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₁ qr) = (inj₁ (leLtTrans po₁ resp₁ (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.reflexive (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁) pe) qr))
  -- Case 2, subcase 2b: q₁ ≈₁ r₁ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂. From p₁ ≈₁ q₁ and q₁ ≈₁ r₁, transitivity of ≈₁ gives p₁ ≈₁ r₁. From p₂ ≤₂ q₂ and q₂ ≤₂ r₂, transitivity of ≤₂ gives p₂ ≤₂ r₂. So p ≤ₗₑₓ r via the second disjunct.
  ×-lex-trans po₁ resp₁ trans₂ (inj₂ (pe , pl)) (inj₂ (qe , ql)) = (inj₂ (IsEquivalence.trans (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po₁)) pe qe , trans₂ pl ql))

You are a mathematician writing informal proofs that will later be formalised
in Agda by another agent. Write in ordinary mathematical English. Do not write
Agda. Do not skip steps by saying "clearly" or "trivially".


Follow the format of these examples exactly.

### Example 1

Informal statement:
For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-identityr : (n : Nat) → n + 0 ≡ n

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + 0 reduces to 0, so the two sides are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: suppose n + 0 = n. Then (suc n) + 0 reduces to suc (n + 0),
and rewriting with the induction hypothesis turns this into suc n.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 2

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers m and n, m + suc n = suc (m + n).

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-suc : (m n : Nat) → m + suc n ≡ suc (m + n)

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on m, holding n fixed.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + suc n reduces to suc n, and suc (0 + n) also reduces to suc n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + suc n = suc (m + n). Then (suc m) + suc n reduces
to suc (m + suc n), which by the induction hypothesis equals suc (suc (m + n)),
which is suc ((suc m) + n).
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 3

Informal statement:
Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-comm : (m n : Nat) → m + n ≡ n + m

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="lemma" name="plusZeroRight">
First we need that n + 0 = n for every n; this is a separate induction and we
record it as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="plusSucRight">
We also need that m + suc n = suc (m + n) for all m and n; again a separate
induction, recorded as its own lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="induction">
Now argue by induction on m.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + n reduces to n, and n + 0 equals n by the first lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + n = n + m. Then suc m + n reduces to suc (m + n),
which by the hypothesis is suc (n + m), which by the second lemma is n + suc m.
</STEP>

private
  variable
    a b ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ℓ₃ ℓ₄ : Level

    B : Set b

-- Definition

-- Properties

              {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} (_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄) →

              (Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_) ⇒ (×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_)

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_

  ×-transitive : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Transitive _≤₂_ →
                 Transitive _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-transitive po₁ trans₂ =
    Strict.×-transitive {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
      isEquivalence (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ isEquivalence ≤-resp-≈)
      (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁)
      trans₂
    where open IsPartialOrder po₁

  ×-decidable : Decidable _≈₁_ → Decidable _≤₁_ → Decidable _≤₂_ →
                Decidable _≤ₗₑₓ_

    Strict.×-decidable dec-≈₁ (Conv.<-decidable _ _ dec-≈₁ dec-≤₁)
                       dec-≤₂

module _ {_≈₁_ : Rel A ℓ₁} {_≤₁_ : Rel A ℓ₂}
         {_≈₂_ : Rel B ℓ₃} {_≤₂_ : Rel B ℓ₄}
         where

  private
    _≤ₗₑₓ_ = ×-Lex _≈₁_ _≤₁_ _≤₂_
    _≋_    = Pointwise _≈₁_ _≈₂_

  ×-antisymmetric : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → Antisymmetric _≈₂_ _≤₂_ →
                   Antisymmetric _≋_ _≤ₗₑₓ_
  ×-antisymmetric po₁ antisym₂ =
    Strict.×-antisymmetric {_≈₁_ = _≈₁_} {_<₂_ = _≤₂_}
       ≈-sym₁ irrefl₁ asym₁ antisym₂
    where
    open IsPartialOrder po₁
    open Eq renaming (refl to ≈-refl₁; sym to ≈-sym₁)

    irrefl₁ : Irreflexive _≈₁_ (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    irrefl₁ = Conv.<-irrefl _≈₁_ _≤₁_

    asym₁ : Asymmetric (Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_)
    asym₁ = trans∧irr⇒asym {_≈_ = _≈₁_}
                           ≈-refl₁ (Conv.<-trans _ _ po₁) irrefl₁

  ×-respects₂ : IsEquivalence _≈₁_ →
                _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → _≤₂_ Respects₂ _≈₂_ →
                _≤ₗₑₓ_ Respects₂ _≋_

    Strict.×-respects₂ eq₁ (Conv.<-resp-≈ _ _ eq₁ resp₁) resp₂


------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structures

  -- dsp: lemmas
  ltLeTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a b → b ≤₁ c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- 1. By definition, a <₁ b means a ≤₁ b and not (a ≈₁ b).
  -- 2. From a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c, transitivity of ≤₁ gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first part of a <₁ c.
  -- 3. It remains to show not (a ≈₁ c). We argue by contradiction, so assume a ≈₁ c.
  -- 4. By symmetry of ≈₁, the assumption a ≈₁ c gives c ≈₁ a.
  -- 5. We have b ≤₁ c and c ≈₁ a. Since ≤₁ respects ≈₁ on the right, these give b ≤₁ a.
  -- 6. We now have a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ a. By antisymmetry of the partial order, a ≈₁ b.
  -- 7. This contradicts the fact from step 1 that not (a ≈₁ b). So the assumption a ≈₁ c is false.
  -- 8. Hence not (a ≈₁ c). Together with a ≤₁ c from step 2, this gives a <₁ c.
  ltLeTrans po resp (a≤b , a≉b) b≤c = (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → a≉b (IsPartialOrder.antisym po a≤b (resp .proj₁ (IsEquivalence.sym (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.isEquivalence (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po)) z) b≤c))))

  leLtTrans : IsPartialOrder _≈₁_ _≤₁_ → _≤₁_ Respects₂ _≈₁_ → {a b c : A} → a ≤₁ b → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ b c → Conv._<_ _≈₁_ _≤₁_ a c
  -- Step 1: by definition, b <₁ c means b ≤₁ c and not (b ≈₁ c). We record both facts for use below.
  leLtTrans po resp a≤b (b≤c , b≉c) =
    -- Step 2: transitivity of ≤₁ applied to a ≤₁ b and b ≤₁ c gives a ≤₁ c. This is the first component needed for a <₁ c.
    (Relation.Binary.Structures.IsPreorder.trans (IsPartialOrder.isPreorder po) a≤b b≤c , (λ z → b≉c (IsPartialOrder.antisym po b≤c (resp .proj₂ z a≤b))))
